title: Run ERC before solver-backed analysis
text: Before claiming a circuit is ready for solver-backed analysis, run circuit_run_erc and inspect the machine-readable result. Treat ERC errors as blockers. Warnings require a short explanation. If the user is sketching and asks for design help, ERC findings may be used as guidance rather than a hard stop.

title: Prefer instrument nodes over a fixed bench
text: The preferred lab workflow is node-based test equipment. Place scopes, meters, and later signal generators directly on the schematic, wire their pins like components, and open their instrument panel from the node. Floating instrument windows are preferred because the user likes test equipment on other monitors. Docking can be offered later as an option.

title: Keep component provenance separate from sourcing
text: Do not treat marketplace listings as verified component specifications. The component model separates archetypes, part families, manufacturer parts, datasheet claims, and sourcing records. When the agent ingests or suggests a component, it should preserve confidence and provenance instead of collapsing everything into one unverified part.

title: Use filesystem storage for electronics knowledge
text: This electronics prototype uses the ordinary filesystem for cards, project memory, generated run artifacts, and assistant discovery. Do not use Suite VFS storage in this app. If Suite integration happens later, keep the filesystem-backed card source of truth portable.

title: Build, place and test a programmable component
text: A programmable component is a reusable part whose behaviour is a FRust node program, backed by a definition in the open project; each instance has its own state. workbench_capabilities (section programmable) lists the definitions, the component node types and the tools. Workflow: 1. component_list (reuse a definition if one fits). 2. component_create with pins (roles), parameters and state. 3. component_open_program and node_program_* to build the behaviour: read pins (pc_pin_voltage), time, parameters and state; decide with ordinary nodes (gt, lt, if, arithmetic; there is no boolean and/or node, so combine conditions by chaining if nodes, and put every condition the requirement names in the graph); drive pins (pc_drive, pc_set_resistance, pc_drive_current) and keep memory with pc_state_set. 4. node_program_validate and component_compile; fix the errors. 5. component_place and schematic_connect into a test circuit with the loads and supplies the part expects. 6. Simulate with analytics_operating_point or analytics_transient and compare with the behaviour expected by hand (levels, thresholds, timing). 7. Any value that differs from the requirement means it is not done: change, compile and simulate again; report success only when every checked value matches. Pins can be added, renamed (keep the uid) and removed later with component_update; wires on renamed pins stay. For a user who wants to design it by hand, component_place with no name places a blank component; they double-click it to open the Node Designer and its Component panel.
